messages:
morgan: Heads-up — Elmwood Health onboarding: we're seeing intermittent tail latency spikes (95th) and higher token spend vs our baseline. They have a renewal conversation in ~2 weeks; flagged as moderate risk if we don't reduce latency/cost. Thinking a proactive play: run an int8 quant swap on their primary route + a RW-compact fallback for heavy tails, with a small canary and routing policy. Any concerns?

dana: Ack. Do we have concrete perf / quality numbers to share with them? they usually want CTAs and numbers.

morgan: Quick bench numbers from lab: int8 on rw-econ-v1 -> ~28% cost/token reduction, median latency ~12ms lower, 95th ~120ms lower on similar request mix. Eval on Elmwood's prompt subset shows ~0.6% FP increase (small).

rajeev: Sounds promising. My recommendation: canary inside their Dedicated pool (so we don't cross-customer blast radius). Start at 5% traffic, ramp to 25% over 48h. Autoscale routing: if quality regresses >1% on sampled prompts OR 95th latency increases >10ms vs baseline, automatically rollback. Also add an explicit fallback route to rw-compact-v2 for requests hitting the tail.

erin: OK from an ops SLA standpoint. Need a clear rollback SLA and monitoring hooks. Add a CS-sampled prompt accuracy metric (we can ingest a tiny labeled set from Elmwood). If those checks fail, rollback immediately and notify P0.

morgan: Draft rollout config (example):
```json
{
  "route": "elmwood-primary",
  "canary": {
    "model": "rw-econ-v1",
    "quant": "int8",
    "start_pct": 5,
    "target_pct": 25,
    "ramp": "48h"
  },
  "fallback": {
    "model": "rw-compact-v2",
    "policy": "auto-on-tail"
  },
  "rollback_conditions": [
    "sampled_prompt_accuracy_drop>1%",
    "95th_latency_delta_ms>10"
  ]
}
```

dana: I'll take the owner role for customer comms and enablement. Plan: ask Elmwood for a 1-hour window for initial canary, run internal demo, then start canary. Also want to capture qualitative feedback via a 1-question quick survey after 24h. I'll draft the note to their PO (@jen) and share here.

rajeev: Two small implementation notes: enable prefix caching for this route (helps conversational tails), and override batching to batch_size=8 for better throughput on int8 kernels. I'll add those as route overrides.

morgan: Owners + timeline: dana (CS owner, customer comms), rajeev (implementation), erin (monitoring/rollback runbook). I'll spin up a tiny dashboard with: 95th latency, median latency, token cost delta, sampled accuracy, and canary percent. Posting link once ready. @cs_bot can you create a CS ticket for tracking?

cs_bot: Ticket created: CS-10123 — "Elmwood Health: int8 canary + fallback rollout". Assigned to dana; linked to ENG-20234 for implementation.

erin: Scheduling note: canary start proposed Mon 09:00 UTC. I'll block the window and add alert playbook to the runbook (rollback play attached).

morgan: Thanks everyone. Dana — when you have the customer window, paste the short script we'll run and the expected rollback criteria in the email. I'll also attach the dashboard and the eval numbers.

dana: Will do. Draft going out in ~30m. Will capture customer feedback and post results here after 24h.

morgan: Perfect. If the canary looks good, plan to finish ramp and then propose a renewal note highlighting cost/latency wins.

erin: Noted. I'll keep an eye on 95th and the sampled prompts.

morgan: (action) rajeev — please prepare the batch/kv caching override PR and tag ENG-20234. dana — customer comms. erin — monitoring hooks.

rajeev: On it — will PR today and include a bench command snippet for the team.

morgan: Thanks — ping me on slack if anything blocks.
